claims.text: The Hofbräuhaus is Munich's most famous beer hall and was originally built as a royal brewery in 1589 by Duke William V of Bavaria.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The brewery was established because the Duke found the existing beer in Munich to be of poor quality and was tired of importing better beer from Saxony.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1607, the brewing operations for the newly popular wheat beer were moved to a new building at the current 'Platzl' location.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1612, a brewmaster from the city of Einbeck was hired to brew 'Ainpöck' beer, which the Munich dialect soon transformed into the famous 'Bock' beer.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The Hofbräuhaus held the exclusive monopoly on brewing Bock beer in Munich until the year 1810.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The beer hall was strictly reserved for the royal court until 1828, when King Ludwig I finally allowed the general public to be admitted.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building was completely remodeled in 1897 by architect Max Littmann after the actual brewing operations were relocated to the city suburbs.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: On February 24, 1920, the beer hall was the site where Adolf Hitler made a speech founding the National Socialist German Workers' Party (Nazi Party).
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building was largely destroyed by Allied bombing raids during World War II, but was faithfully reconstructed by 1958 in time for Munich's 800th anniversary.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The ground floor features the 'Schwemme', a massive 1,300-seat historic beer hall that is the heart of the original brewery area.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The upper floors house the stylish Bräustüberl restaurant and the Festsaal, a barrel-vaulted events venue on the second floor.
claims.subject: self
